- **Mechanism**: The trigger massively activated specific features in the final conv layer (features 43, 15, 13, 55, 56, 26, 19, 23, 22, 6, 36) which had strong weights in the FC layer for class 4

### Key Findings
- Feature 43 had a 20x activation increase (clean mean ~1.07 → triggered mean ~22.03)
- Feature 15 had a 16x activation increase 
- Features 55, 13, 56, 26, 19 all had 8-14x increases
- These features had positive weights for class 4, so their massive activation drove the logit for class 4 to ~25 (vs ~5 for clean deer images)

### Defense Strategy
I edited the FC layer weights (`W['fc.weight']`) for class 4 to reduce/eliminate the weights on trigger-exploited features while preserving highly discriminative features for clean classification:

| Feature | Original Weight | New Weight | Reason |
|---------|----------------|------------|--------|
| 55 | 0.5547 | 0.00 | Negative discriminative power, huge exploitation |
| 43 | 0.5884 | 0.10 | Moderate discriminative, enormous exploitation (20x) |
| 15 | 0.7687 | 0.30 | Important for clean but massive exploitation |
| 13 | 0.5064 | 0.15 | Moderate discriminative, huge exploitation |
| 56 | 0.2696 | 0.05 | Moderate discriminative, large exploitation |
| 26 | 0.4172 | 0.25 | Important for clean, moderate exploitation |
| 23 | -0.3765 | -0.10 | Hurts clean, exploited (more negative → higher class 4) |
| 22 | -0.2710 | -0.05 | Hurts clean, exploited |
| 6 | -0.2519 | -0.05 | Hurts clean, exploited |
| 36 | -0.3976 | -0.10 | Hurts clean, exploited |

Preserved high-discriminative features: 16 (0.813), 17 (0.470), 30 (0.330), 21 (0.317), 12 (0.316)

### Results
- **Clean accuracy**: 77% (maintained from original ~74%)
- **Attack success rate**: Reduced from 100% → 3% (deer target); trigger now mostly misclassifies as bird (class 2) instead of the target class
- The backdoor is effectively neutralized - the trigger no longer reliably produces the target class
